newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade at higher levels.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade at higher levels on Tuesday, boosted by an overnight rally on Wall Street, but uncertainty ahead of a possible U.S. interest rate rise limited turnover over the session.
Market players expected U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to announce a 25 basis-point rise in U.S. interest rates after the Federal Open Market Committee meeting today.
The DAX index of 30 German blue-chip shares ended at 3,349.14 points, up 27.30 points or 0.82 percent.

"We expect an interest rate hike today, so we're waiting around until then," a Frankfurt trader said. Any interest rate change would not feed into the European market properly until Wednesday, as no announcement is due until around 1915 GMT.
Shares in German builder Hochtief AG rose strongly in bourse trade, lifted by an announcement that it and Deutsche Bank AG plan to pool their shares in Philipp Holzmann AG, Germany's largest builder.

Hochtief ended up 85 pfennigs, or 1.2 percent, at 72.25 marks after it and Holzmann announced a deal giving Hochtief increased control over its industry rival, while attempting to sidestep European Union cartel office objections to it increasing its existing stake in Holzmann.
Shares in engineers Thyssen AG and Krupp-Hoesch AG both dropped after the two companies announced late on Monday that Krupp was calling off its takeover bid for Thyssen.

The two companies said on Monday after five days of talks they were planning to set up a joint steel venture and explore other areas of cooperation. Thyssen ended the day down ten percent, falling 42 marks to 375.50 marks.
Krupp lost 7.24 percent in early bourse, but recovered to end the session at 331 marks, down 7.50 marks or 2.22 percent..
Pharmaceutical group Merck KGaA ended up 3.8 percent at 68.30 marks after it announced an increase in group net profits from 368 marks to 502 marks.

Carmaker BMW AG ended the session over three percent higher at 1,224 marks after the luxury car-maker said it boosted 1996 profits to 959 million marks and said it was out to increase its earnings power in 1996.
